ops.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. CLAUDE FOR SMALL BUSINESS (13 May 2026): Anthropic shipped a packaged SMB offering — 15 agentic workflows plus 15 reusable skills and connectors to QuickBooks, PayPal, HubSpot, Canva, DocuSign, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and Slack, running through Claude Cowork. No surcharge beyond existing Claude licences and whatever partner tools a business already pays for; a 10-city US AI-fluency tour began 14 May. This lands squarely on the solo-/lean-team segment SageReasoning occupies and is directly relevant to the founder's own dogfooding stack. SOLO-FOUNDER ECONOMICS: A Fortune piece (18 May) documents solo founders running entire-team workloads on AI while candidly flagging the limits of going alone (judgment, accountability, burnout) — alongside the standing data that solo-founded US startups reached ~36.3% of new companies by mid-2025 and a full agent stack runs ~$300–$500/month (≈$3K–$12K/year) versus equivalent headcount. FUNDING: Carta's State of Pre-Seed Q1 2026 is confirmed — ~3,000 US startups raised ~$2.3B (expected to settle ~$2.9B); AI now takes ~50% of pre-seed dollars and ~33% of total VC; AI seed valuations carry a ~42% premium (median pre-money ~$17.9M). The $1M–$2.5M band shrank to 18% of rounds (from 24% in 2023) — a barbell market. REGULATION: EU Digital Omnibus (7 May provisional deal) remains in legal-linguistic revision; formal Council/Parliament adoption must complete before 2 Aug 2026 or original Annex III dates re-activate. Australia's first mandatory AI-policy requirement begins 15 June 2026 (~3 weeks out). US: the Dec 2025 federal-preemption executive order and California EO N-5-26 (30 Mar) signal a contested state/federal patchwork, though child-safety and government-procurement carve-outs are shielded from preemption. RISKS: Omnibus adoption slip past 2 Aug; AU 15 June proximity. OPPORTUNITY: Claude for Small Business may sharpen the founder's own Sage Ops tooling at near-zero marginal cost.

tech.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. ANTHROPIC: Opus 4.7 remains GA (since 16 Apr) at $5/$25 per million tokens. Claude Code rate limits were doubled and Opus API limits raised. Managed Agents on the Claude Platform gained Dreaming (reviews past sessions to improve memory) and multi-agent orchestration (a lead agent delegating to parallel specialist sub-agents on a shared filesystem) — both relevant to any future Sage Ops/agent build. The Batches API now supports up to 300k output tokens via the output-300k-2026-03-24 beta header. SONNET 4.8: still unannounced as of 23 May — no model card, API id, or benchmarks; the source-map 'leak' is now widely doubted and a 4.6→4.8 skip would be unprecedented. Treat as rumour, not roadmap. SUPABASE: Pricing unchanged (Free / $25 Pro / $599 Team / Enterprise). New shipping relevant to SageReasoning's P4 Stripe wiring: a one-click Stripe Sync Engine that mirrors customers, subscriptions, and invoices into Postgres, plus an Index Advisor (auto-flags missing indexes), AI table filters, Supabase Warehouse, and Multigres sharding. SECURITY — AUTH/ENCRYPTION: CVE-2026-40372 (ASP.NET Core Data Protection elevation-of-privilege, CVSS 9.1) — the authenticated encryptor computed its HMAC over the wrong bytes, allowing forged auth cookies and SYSTEM-level access. CVE-2026-41940 (cPanel/WHM authentication-bypass, CVSS 9.8) is mass-exploited in the wild. May Patch Tuesday spanned ~118–132 CVEs. The Next.js May release (15.5.18 / 16.2.6; 13 advisories incl. SSRF CVE-2026-44578) is now ~3 weeks old and should already be patched on any self-hosted path. LLM COSTS: the Cache→Route→Compress framing is now standard; prompt caching cuts cached-input cost up to ~90%, full-stack optimisation 70–90%. RISKS — FOUNDER ATTENTION: confirm no exposure to the ASP.NET Core / cPanel CVEs; verify Next.js is patched. OPPORTUNITY: Supabase's Stripe Sync Engine could materially simplify P4.

growth.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. AGENT SKILLS MARKETPLACE ECOSYSTEM: The skills/plugins distribution layer matured fast — from one registry in Dec 2025 to ~eight marketplaces by Q2 2026. Notable: Skills.sh (Vercel-backed, npm-style cross-tool CLI installer spanning Claude Code, Codex, Cursor), SkillsMP (~800K GitHub-scraped skills), LobeHub (~169K), and ClaudeSkills.info (free, incl. official Anthropic skills). The SKILL.md format is now an open standard shared across tools. Implication: sage-reason-as-skill has more than one distribution channel; the Anthropic plugin route (Cowork + Code) noted previously is no longer the only path. AGENT EXPERIENCE (AX) / DEVREL SHIFT: The dominant 2026 framing is 'the LLM is your first-touch user' — it consumes your docs and API before any human does. 'API design is a DevRel problem' and 'agent skills are the new demos.' This bears directly on SageReasoning's API-first audience and the llms.txt / agent-card.json discovery surface (P6). COMPETITORS: The guardrails field (Galileo, Bifrost, GA Guard, NeMo, Llama Guard, Lakera) is consolidating around a gateway-enforcement architecture, anchored to the OWASP Top-10-for-LLM taxonomy and the EU AI Act high-risk date (2 Aug 2026). All framing remains governance/security — not virtue ethics — so the differentiation gap, and the brand-confusion exposure on the word 'virtue', is unchanged. STOIC COMMUNITY: The Stoic Arts Conference was held April 2026 at Tufts (with Modern Stoicism); Stoicism Today moved to Substack in 2026; commentary frames the current resurgence ('Stoicism 5.0') as driven by tech/work uncertainty — adjacent to SageReasoning's positioning. Stoicon-X Melbourne remains confirmed for 17 Oct 2026. CONTENT MARKETING: Substack content now surfaces inside ChatGPT/Perplexity/Gemini, making founder-voice thought leadership an AI-discoverable channel. RISKS: marketplace fragmentation raises discovery noise; 'virtue' brand-confusion persists. OPPORTUNITY: AX-first API/skill packaging plus Substack distribution are low-cost, on-theme routes to the agent-developer audience.

support.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. MENTAL-HEALTH AI REGULATION — FEDERAL MOVEMENT: On 5 Mar 2026 House Energy & Commerce advanced a children's online-safety package including the KIDS Act and SAFE BOTs Act — AI disclosure at prescribed cadence, a prohibition on chatbots presenting as licensed professionals, minor-specific protections, and mandatory crisis-resource referral; a separate bill (19 Mar) targets chatbots impersonating doctors/lawyers. State baseline holds: ~11 states / 20 laws by early 2026; 36 states / 70+ chatbot bills in Q1; Illinois and Nevada ban AI for behavioural health; New York's detect-self-harm-and-refer rule remains the de-facto R20a design template. AI-COMPANIONSHIP SENTIMENT: Stanford's 2026 AI Index puts global excitement for AI companionship at 52% (US 42%); analysts forecast 10% of US adults using an AI companion daily by 2027, rising to 30% by 2040. UK public research flags emotional dependency, anthropomorphic deception, and child risk as top concerns and favours regulation — adjacent to R19 (mirror principle) and R20 (relationship asymmetry, independence encouragement). SAFETY INCIDENTS: a May 2026 analysis of ~1,400 AI incidents finds most harm originates in software, not robots; the 2026 Health Tech Hazard Report names AI-chatbot misuse its top hazard; OECD.AI logged further 'reinforce-harmful-behaviour' chatbot incidents. Recurring lesson: anything touching crisis needs safety-by-design, escalation paths, and human routes — echoing the synchronous distress-classifier discipline (PR3). PHILOSOPHICAL COUNSELLING: a WHO-supported workshop (Jan 2026) charted responsible mental-health AI; an adjacent player, Philosophical Health International's free 'Philai' chatbot, now exists; new research links heavy generative-AI use to delusion-like experiences. ACCESSIBILITY: WCAG 2.1 AA stays the live standard (WCAG 3.0 not a mandate before ~2029); Section 504 deadlines remain May 2027/2028. RISK — FOUNDER ATTENTION: firming federal disclosure/impersonation rules are raising the compliance floor SageReasoning's human-facing tools will sit on. OPPORTUNITY: the honest-positioning posture (R18a/R19) aligns with rising public concern.
